verdict.rationale: The GitHub repo documents a free, open-source SigNoz that runs in your own infrastructure via Docker, Kubernetes, or Linux. Community users confirm the self-hosted stack exists and can be deployed (signoz-gh-1, signoz-comm-1, signoz-comm-18). However, users report operational friction: many docker-compose services to reconfigure, more containers than their app, and a failed Windows install. The separately licensed 'ee/' directory also raises an open-core question about whether the full feature set is self-hostable. missing for 10: documented architecture reference for production self-hosting, documented upgrade/migration path between versions, production sizing/HA guidance, independent evidence of production-scale self-hosted operation.
